bill.title: Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Bureau of Land Management relating to Buffalo Field Office Record of Decision and Approved Resource Management Plan Amendment.
bill.officialSummary: This joint resolution nullifies the rule submitted by the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) on November 20, 2024, which amended the 2015 resource management plan (RMP) for the Buffalo Field Office in Wyoming to make no federal coal available for future leasing. Thus, the joint resolution requires the BLM to follow the 2015 RMP as it was before it was amended in 2024 and make coal available for leasing. By way of background, the BLM developed the amendment to the plan in response to Western Organization of Resource Councils v. Bureau of Land Management. In that case, the court held that the BLM must evaluate the climate impacts of federal coal leasing in the Buffalo Field Office and include alternatives to limit or stop coal leasing in the evaluation in order to comply with the National Environmental Policy Act. After conducting the evaluation, the BLM amended the RMP and made BLM-managed coal resources in the Buffalo Field Office planning area unavailable for future leasing.

classification.plainSummary: This joint resolution would overturn a 2024 Bureau of Land Management decision that made federal coal in Wyoming's Buffalo Field Office unavailable for future leasing. If enacted, it would restore the earlier 2015 resource management plan, which allowed coal leasing to continue in that area. The BLM had stopped offering coal leases after a court required the agency to evaluate climate impacts and consider alternatives to coal leasing.

industries.rationale: The bill would directly reopen federal coal resources to leasing, affecting coal extraction companies operating in Wyoming.
Coal mining operations would regain access to federal coal reserves that were made unavailable under the 2024 amendment.
Coal-fired power generators could be affected by changes in the availability and pricing of federal coal supplies.

plain.whatItDoes: This joint resolution would cancel the rule submitted by the federal land agency on November 20, 2024, which amended the 2015 resource management plan for the Buffalo Field Office in Wyoming to make no federal coal available for future leasing.
plain.whoItTouches: People who live near a mine, and people who work in one.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
